title: Groups of Strings
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of strings words, where each string consists of unique lowercase English letters, determine the maximum number of non-intersecting groups the strings can be divided into.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of strings words, where each string consists of unique lowercase English letters, determine the maximum number of non-intersecting groups the strings can be divided into. Each string must either be connected to at least one other string within its group or be the sole string in its group. Connections are made by adding, deleting, or replacing exactly one letter. The result is an array where the first element indicates the maximum number of groups and the second element indicates the size of the largest group.
constraints: Each word contains unique lowercase letters, and letter order does not matter.
Two words connect after exactly one add, delete, or replacement; connectivity is transitive.
Return [number of connected groups, size of the largest group].
hints: Represent each word as a 26-bit set and join directly connected masks.
Deletion toggles one set bit; two masks that produce the same deleted mask differ by one replacement.
Union existing deletion neighbors and keep one representative for each deleted mask; aggregate duplicate words by mask.
Every allowed edit is either one-bit deletion/addition or two masks sharing a one-letter-smaller form, so the unions encode exactly the graph edges.
editorial: Every allowed edit is either one-bit deletion/addition or two masks sharing a one-letter-smaller form, so the unions encode exactly the graph edges.
